just_in.title: Windows 11 Gains Cloud Rebuild: Reinstall From the Cloud Even When the PC Won't Boot
just_in.excerpt: The KB5127936 preview update downloads a Windows image and your drivers from Windows Update — no USB stick needed — but it wipes the system disk, so read the warning first.
just_in.image_caption: A graphic shows a laptop beneath a cloud carrying the Windows logo. Cloud rebuild reinstalls Windows 11 using an image and drivers downloaded from Windows Update, even when the PC cannot start.
just_in.nri_angle: For diaspora tech workers and the family members who are their default IT support, a no-USB rebuild makes rescuing a parent's dead PC a phone-guided job.
just_in.author: Diaspora Desk

steps.step: Install the optional KB5127936 preview update
steps.detail: Settings > Windows Update > Advanced options > Optional updates. The feature rolls out gradually, so it may not appear immediately.

steps.step: Back up anything stored only on the PC
steps.detail: Cloud rebuild reformats the system disk and removes all local files, accounts, apps and settings. Cloud-stored files are unaffected.
If the PC boots: Settings > System > Recovery > Rebuild PC. If it does not: in WinRE, choose Troubleshoot > Recovery and uninstall > Cloud rebuild.
Join Ethernet or Wi-Fi, review the target build, edition and language, and confirm the data-loss warning. Keep the PC plugged in.
"Remove files" is faster; "Remove & sanitize files" is irreversible and is the right choice before selling or handing on the PC.

food.title: For Diwali, Houston Chef Anita Jaisinghani Shares the Traditions — and Her Besan Mithai
food.excerpt: The Pondicheri chef calls Diwali the ultimate family holiday, where sweets are good-luck gifts given with overflowing hands. Her besan mithai — a chickpea fudge — serves 12 and takes 55 minutes.

food.author: Diaspora Desk

steps: Grease a 9-by-13-inch sheet pan and line it with parchment paper.
If using the chocolate topping, melt the chocolate with the heavy cream over a double boiler, stirring frequently, and keep warm.
Heat the ghee in a large saute pan or kadhai.
Add the besan, sugar, cardamom and salt; cook over medium-low heat, stirring constantly, until golden brown with a nutty aroma, 20 to 40 minutes. Do not leave it unattended.
Remove from the heat and immediately spread the mixture onto the prepared pan, smoothing it with an offset spatula.
If topping with chocolate, spread the warm chocolate over it, sprinkle with the pumpkin and sesame seeds, and refrigerate 1 hour to set.
To cut, let the mithai sit at room temperature for 1 hour first, and clean the knife with each cut.
